clue.text: Political theory backing strike — is money after a vote?

indicators.note: after says the word is and the money letter come behind the vote's cross
backing means the word for strike is read from its end to its start

parts.note: to ram is to strike hard
a cross on a ballot paper is a vote

explanation.surface: A question about whether a theory that supports industrial action is really about cash after a ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses the word for strike; 'after' sets the 'is money' letters behind the ballot cross, though they come first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The theory of Karl Marx is the classic political doctrine of class struggle and common ownership.

clue.text: Psychic found between Little and Large

definitions.meaning: a spiritualist who claims to contact the dead
the size between small and large; Little and Large were also a British TV comedy double act

explanation.surface: A clairvoyant discovered standing between the two members of the comedy duo Little and Large.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiritualist go-between is called this, and it is also the middle size on a clothing label.

clue.text: Single file

definitions.meaning: a single is a disc released with one main track
to file is to log or register a document

explanation.surface: Reads as the phrase for walking one behind another in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A vinyl release can be a single, and to file away information is to log it in writing.

clue.text: Run away from fair lot brawling in pubs, causing swellings

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters within the word for pubs

parts.note: inns are pubs

indicators.note: brawling suggests a disorderly scuffle, so the letters are thrown about
away from says the run letter is taken out of the words fair lot

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A crowd at a fair fighting in pubs and running away, leaving people with swollen bruises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like part of the story but is the cricket letter removed by 'away from'; 'brawling' mixes what is left, and 'in' sets it inside the pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflating something makes it puff up, so these are acts of expanding, just as bulges are.

clue.text: Brown tea, after a second

indicators.note: after says the tea word follows the second

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Someone asks for brown tea in just a second.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a coffee-brown colour, named after the dark coffee from the Yemeni port.

clue.text: Laurel's immersed in international books for a moment

indicators.note: immersed in says the comic's name is plunged into the letters that follow

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible
Stan Laurel was the thin half of Laurel and Hardy

explanation.surface: Stan Laurel briefly appearing in an international catalogue of books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'immersed in' sends the comedian into the middle of the books abbreviation, not between the two outer pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A split second, a tiny unit of time, is what this noun denotes.

clue.text: Independent fun girl, over 50, wearing ceremonial clothes

indicators.note: over here means done over, reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An independent-minded, fun-loving woman past fifty who dresses up in formal regalia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is the signal to rework the letters, as in doing something over; the Roman fifty joins the fun girl's letters in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A rig is an outfit, so being fully rigged out means dressed in complete formal costume or uniform.

clue.text: Places alien on board

indicators.note: on, read with board as aboard ship, signals that the alien goes inside the ship letters

parts.note: together with on, board stands for a ship, SS being a steamship
ET is the film alien

explanation.surface: An alien takes his place aboard a spacecraft.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'on board' a ship is a crossword convention for going inside SS (steamship).
explanation.definitionFit: To set something down is to place or position it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Queen kidnapped by disturbed maniac, one from abroad?

indicators.note: kidnapped by puts the royal letters inside the jumbled word
disturbed means the word maniac is mixed up

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline about the Queen seized by a deranged foreign madman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' scrambles the maniac and 'kidnapped by' holds the royal cipher inside the result; the question mark flags that abroad depends on where you stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen from Britain, a citizen of the United States is a foreigner from across the Atlantic, hence the question mark.

clue.text: She hates revision for a series of tests

indicators.note: a revision reworks something, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl who loathes revising for her exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tests' are cricket Test matches: the Ashes is the famous England v Australia Test series.
explanation.definitionFit: The trophy contested by England and Australia is decided by a series of five-day cricket Test matches.

clue.text: Met over coffee

indicators.note: over means the word for met is turned round

parts.note: faced means confronted, met

explanation.surface: Two people met for a chat over a cup of coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A short name for caffeine-free coffee, a common order in cafes.

clue.text: Brew fierce tea, but not with this!

definitions.text: Brew fierce tea, but not with this!

indicators.note: to brew is to stir up or concoct, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A warning: make your strong tea, but don't use this gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a French press is a coffee pot, so it is not for brewing tea.
explanation.definitionFit: This plunger pot is made for coffee, which is why one should not brew tea in it.

clue.text: Like a good poker player's bad handwriting?

definitions.text: Like a good poker player's bad handwriting?

parts.words: Like a good poker player's bad handwriting?
parts.note: a good poker player keeps an expressionless face that gives nothing away, and bad handwriting cannot be deciphered; one adjective covers both

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a card shark's scrawl is as hard to decipher as his face.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegible scrawl and an impassive poker face share the quality of giving nothing away to the observer.

clue.text: Stories of heartless people

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the five-letter word is removed

parts.note: lives can mean people, as in many lives were lost

explanation.surface: Tales of cruel, unfeeling people.
explanation.walkthrough: LIVES loses its middle letter, V.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories can mean fibs or untruths, the sense of a child telling stories.

clue.text: Discipline at the bottom of Tory superego

indicators.note: in a down entry at the bottom of puts the discipline word below the Tory one

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, a Tory
a science is a discipline, a field of study

explanation.surface: Discipline as the foundation of a Conservative's moral sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud's superego is the inner moral censor, the voice that tells us right from wrong.

clue.text: Hell, belonging to a firm is immaterial

parts.note: Dis is the Roman underworld, or Dante's city in Hell
corporate means of a company or firm

explanation.surface: Working for a company is hell and doesn't matter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be without a body is to be bodiless, incorporeal, with no physical substance.

clue.text: I'm a cool fan touring Britain, north and south 7

definitions.note: 7 down is American, so this means a South American

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the jumbled letters enclose the Britain letter
to fan is to spread out, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cool fan travelling round Britain, from top to bottom, who hails from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fan' turns I'MACOOL into COLOMIA; 'touring' puts B inside it, then N follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Colombia, a country of northern South America, is a South American.

clue.text: 2 down grasps theory, oddly strained

indicators.note: grasps means the cross-reference letters hold the chosen letters inside

parts.note: 2 down's clue gives file as one of its two meanings

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters of theory

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for down in crossword cross-references

explanation.surface: A cross-reference grips a theory that is oddly forced.
explanation.walkthrough: '2 down' is split: the 2 gives one meaning of that clue, file, and down gives its abbreviation; 'grasps' then holds the odd letters picked by 'oddly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid that has been passed through a sieve or mesh has been strained.

clue.text: Are they a treat I'm chewing?

definitions.text: Are they a treat I'm chewing?

indicators.note: chewing mashes things up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone munching biscuits asks whether these are a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: almond biscuits are a treat to chew.
explanation.definitionFit: These Italian almond macaroons are a sweet treat eaten with coffee.

clue.text: 1-2000 doctors losing out to medical specialist

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral 1 and MM is 2000

indicators.note: doctors as a verb means tampers with, so these letters are altered

explanation.surface: A thousand-strong body of doctors losing ground to a specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor who studies the body's defences against infection is a specialist in that branch of medicine.

clue.text: Logician grasps 1 across in capital

indicators.note: grasps means the logician's name holds the numeral inside

parts.note: John Venn, of Venn diagrams, was a logician
I is the Roman numeral one
A is the abbreviation for across in crossword cross-references

explanation.surface: A logician gets to grips with the first across answer in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 across' is not the cross-reference it seems: it gives I + A, with I inside VENN.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria's capital city is on the Danube.

clue.text: How one might kiss Dawn?

definitions.meaning: a kiss with open mouths takes its name from France
Dawn ... is a British comedian, of The Vicar of Dibley

explanation.definitionFit: An open-mouthed kiss takes its name from France, and Dawn French is a famous British comic actor.

clue.text: Anatolian country follows Trump's lead over head of Russia

indicators.note: follows says the country comes after Trump's first letter
lead means the first letter of Trump's
over means the country covers the next letter, going round it

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom, is a country

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of Russia

explanation.surface: A political headline: a country falls in line behind Trump rather than Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatolia is the Asian heartland of Turkey, so an Anatolian is a native of that country.

clue.text: Muesli prepared with fire and food additive

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, worked up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A breakfast cereal cooked over a fire, with something added to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance such as lecithin that keeps oil and water mixed is a common additive in processed food.

clue.text: 27 Italy's past includes Tango

definitions.note: 27 across begins with drink, so this reads as Italy's drink

indicators.note: includes means the word for past takes the letter inside

parts.note: late means former, past
T is Tango in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Italy's past containing the tango dance.
explanation.walkthrough: '27' points to 27 across, whose first word is DRINK, so the definition is Italy's drink.
explanation.definitionFit: This milky coffee is a classic Italian beverage, its name meaning milk.

clue.text: Hard to understand when BBC drama axes the first three characters

indicators.note: axes the first three characters means the opening three letters of the drama's title are cut

parts.note: Poldark is a BBC period drama set in Cornwall

explanation.surface: A puzzling BBC drama that cuts its opening characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like the cast but means letters: POLDARK loses POL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscure or mysterious is said to be shadowy, unclear in meaning.

clue.text: High church member's 'Spiritual Is Theological' piece

definitions.note: the 's reads as is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: piece means only part of the quoted title is used

explanation.surface: An Anglo-Catholic writing an article titled 'Spiritual Is Theological'.
explanation.definitionFit: A believer devoted to elaborate ceremonial worship, as in the Anglo-Catholic wing of the Church of England.

clue.text: President exchanges vote for new fabric

indicators.note: exchanges vote for new means the voting cross is swapped for the new letter

parts.note: Richard Nixon was a US President
X is a cross on a ballot, a vote

explanation.surface: A president trades his vote for a new kind of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sheer lightweight silk or chiffon-like material, named after the courtesan Ninon de Lenclos.

clue.text: Appreciate case of red knocked back at home with family

indicators.note: knocked back means the two letters are turned round, as one knocks back a drink
case of means the outer letters of red

parts.note: in means at home
kin are family

explanation.surface: Enjoying a case of red wine downed at home with the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' gives RD, and 'knocked back' turns it to DR.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb something eagerly, such as a view or atmosphere, is to take it all in and savour it.

clue.text: Hair found in Keith's ale? Yes, it's returned

indicators.note: returned means those letters run backwards
found in means the letters are sitting inside the words Keith's ale? Yes

explanation.surface: Someone finds a hair floating in Keith's pint and sends it back.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'Keith's ale? Yes' backwards gives SEYELASHTIEK, with the answer in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the short hairs fringing the eyelid is a single hair of this kind.
